new_statements.relation_note: Catalog rule for Davaweño is empty and there are no existing statements; this wordlist supplies the first primary data on record: 13 stress-marked forms, all penultimate, from the 'Islam' (Muslim Kalagan) Davaweño of Piso/Mapoti, Banaybanay, Davao Oriental. Low weight: it is a 1971 field wordlist with no phonological statement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule is stated. The fieldworker marked primary stress with a raised tick before the stressed syllable on 13 of 372 entries (the typed list uses q for glottal stop, so the tick is unambiguously a stress mark, e.g. word-initial in 'lawas, 'gɨtɨm, 'bagaq). Every one of the 13 marked forms has the stress on the penultimate syllable: 'la.was, pa.'ra.ngay, ko.'ko.on, 'gɨ.tɨm, bi.'ti.is, kɨ.'ga.oq, 'ba.gaq, ba.'ri.ka, ma.'mu.ruq, ma.ga.'la.a, sə.'lo.pan, kag.'wa.ngan. Item 238 'river' ləwas is flagged as a minimal contrast with 'lawas 'body' (the contrast is at least in the vowel, ə vs a; the body word additionally carries the stress tick). This is raw field data, not a description: it supports penultimate stress in the marked items only and says nothing about the other 359 entries.
new_statements.exceptions: none; all marked forms are penultimate. Why only these 13 were marked is not explained (several have identical vowels in adjacent syllables, where the tick disambiguates which one is stressed).
new_statements.identity_note: Both works are SIL Philippines 'Expanded Philippine Word List' (1966 master list) elicitations labelled 'Kalagan - Davaweño/Davawenyo' from Piso (and Mapoti), Banaybanay, Davao Oriental, and both are filed by SIL under Kalagan [kqe] rather than Davawenyo [daw]. Work 1 is explicitly the 'Islam' (Muslim) community's speech ('ISLAM: piso' banaybanay.. mapoti' banaybanay, Davao Oriental', 11/10/71). The two lists differ noticeably in vocabulary and vowel inventory (the 1971 list has the barred-i/schwa vowels ɨ, ə; the 1973-74 list writes e/ĕ), so they may represent two Mansakan varieties along the Kalagan-Davaweño boundary; the catalog entry 'Davaweño' should be understood as Kalagan-Davaweño of Banaybanay on the strength of these sources.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every component of the stitched deciding quote is in the Zorc 1977 text we hold layer at the stated locators (Table 3 item 11, 2.3.2, 3.1.3, fn.70), verbatim modulo scanned letter-spacing; Zorc 1977 contains no accent statement for Davaweño, exactly as the record says, and our earlier survey/the first reading attribution of the Bisayan accent rule to Davaweño was a misreading that A/B already corrected. (2) The deciding source is a 1977 comparative-historical dissertation in which Davaweño is a comparison variety; but no dedicated description of Davawenyo phonology exists: Glottolog 5.1 lists one descriptive work (Lee 2004, clitic ordering), and an open-web search (Wikipedia/Mansakan refs, zorc.net Mansakan folder, ANU repository, SIL Philippines archive, Iglesia et al. 2024 archival survey) found only SIL wordlists (1971, 1973-74) and a 1973 text, Gallman 1979 (subgrouping only, downloaded
